To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We propose a novel cross device and/or domain SCA attack methodology based on meta transfer learning.
we propose a novel meta transfer learning based cross device profiling SCA attack that can break AES-128 encryption engines on a profiling device using only one or two traces from a target device.
we propose the first cross-device and/or cross-domain side-channel attacks based on meta transfer learning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new attack mechanism for cross device and/or domain SCA attacks, which has not been considered before.

the following questions: Can we use meta transfer learning to train a cross device SCA model with a profiling device? Can we apply our method to cross device attacks in different side channel sources, e.g., power and EM? Can we reduce the training cost and number of traces required for SCA?

the following contributions:
1. We propose a novel cross device SCA attack mechanism based on the meta transfer learning framework.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our attack methodology is able to transfer a DL network trained on one device to another device, even with a different side channel source.
the proposed attack methodology is the first to demonstrate that a meta transfer learning approach can be successfully applied to SCA attacks.
we have developed a cross device and cross domain side channel attack methodology using a profiling device to attack a target device.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to successfully break AES-128 with 1000 traces on the profiling device and 5000 traces on the target devices.
we are able to achieve 100% success rates in cross device and cross domain profiling side channel attacks with a small number of traces.
our method enables the adversary to perform a cross device and cross domain SCA on the target devices with only one profiling device.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we show that a meta learning based approach can effectively transfer knowledge among target devices, which can be used in cross-device SCA attacks, and thus can significantly reduce the number of traces required for SCA attack.
meta transfer learning can be used as a powerful tool to transfer DL models among different devices, even when different side channel sources are used.
meta transfer learning can be applied to SCA to reduce data and training costs.
